Subject: Hosted API pricing inquiry and forecast

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. We ran the forecast for our new recommendation engine and expect ~1.2B tokens/month after ramp (peak Q1). Procurement asked me to get a clear picture of per-token pricing and any available commit tiers you can offer for hosted API consumption.

Attached is a short exec summary and the token forecast. Two asks: (1) the tiered per-token rates for 1M -> 1B+ monthly usage, and (2) any available credits/discounts we can stack with annual commit or prepay. We have a standard procurement calendar — want to finalize commercials by Oct 20.

Appreciate your help,
Sarah
Sarah Wong
Head of Platform, BrightLayer AI

Attachments: BrightLayer_MA_Exec_Summary.pdf, usage_forecast_sheet.xlsx

Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing inquiry and forecast

Hi Sarah — great to hear the ramp looks healthy. Thanks for the materials. I pulled together an initial hosted-tier proposal and a couple of options depending on commit structure. See the attached proposed_rate_table_v2.csv for the two paths: (A) pure usage slabs (monthly per-token) and (B) 12‑month commit with blended unit pricing plus a small prepay credit.

High level ask for you: which commercial path looks closest to your procurement constraints (monthly flexibility vs. 12‑month commit)? If you can share the expected distribution across Q1 (tokens by month), we can tighten the numbers.

I also want to escalate one ask internally: BrightLayer is requesting a deeper than usual break at the 800M monthly token mark (a 25% off list step) which sits outside our standard rate card. If we pursue that, I need approval from Pricing/Revenue. Karthik/Marissa — looping you in to flag that this could be a custom slab approval request.

Next steps: Sarah — I can book 30 mins this week to walk through the two approaches and the attachments.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing inquiry and forecast

Lauren — thanks for the context and the ask. Quick thoughts:

- Rate card baseline: our published slabs already provide step-downs at 100M, 250M, 500M, 1B. A 25% ad hoc off-list at 800M is material and needs documented justification (strategic customer, expected ARR, multi-year commit).
- Approval path: Pricing can approve partial deviation up to 10% if there's a signed 12‑month commit >= $X (internal threshold). Anything beyond that should go through Revenue Committee + Finance sign-off.
- Recommended compromise: offer 12‑month commit at 850M/mo with a blended per-token that nets ~12% off list and include a 10% prepay credit if BrightLayer prepays 50% upfront. That keeps us within guardrails and gives the customer a meaningful delta vs list.

If Marissa signs off on the approach I can draft the supporting economics (unit cost, margin sensitivity) for Finance. Include the proposed attachments and the HubSpot deal link in the submission.

Karthik
Director, Pricing & Revenue Operations

- Karthik — prepare the margin sensitivity and the finance packet (I need to see net contribution and incremental cost with our quantized runtime assumptions).
- Lauren — you can present this to Sarah as our official commercial path; flag that final approval is contingent on Finance sign-off and legal’s standard T&Cs (no change in data residency).

Marissa Cole

Hi Sarah — following internal review, we can present a formal commercial that balances rate-card discipline and your scale:

Option A (Flex monthly): standard published slabs (best for variability)
Option B (12‑month commit): 850M/month committed; blended per‑token price that results in ~12% off list across expected consumption; 10% prepay credit if 50% of the year is prepaid up front.

We are saving a custom 25% breakpoint ask at 800M for larger exec review (Revenue Committee) — for now this is the path most likely to execute quickly. See attached for the exact numbers and a simple NPV model.

Can you confirm which path you prefer by Oct 15 so our legal and procurement teams can prepare the SOW? If you want, we can lock a short call next week to walk through the numbers.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

If those are acceptable, we should be able to move to a redline-ready commercial by Oct 18.

Sarah
